surface noun

also on the surface, the surface of the water, come to the surface

classical

Plaut. Cas. 2.6.33: in aquā summā natāre (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fin. 4.64: ad aquam summam appropinquāre (Lewis & Short)

summus, summa, summum

adjective, with the noun: summa aqua, the surface of the water · Declension on Wiktionary

the top of, the surface of

Latin says “the top water” as it says “the top of the mountain” (summus mōns): the adjective agrees with the thing. As a noun, summum is the top or surface (ā summō, Cic. Fin. 3.48). Its other senses are highest, greatest, last (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • superficiēs, superficiēī f. — the upper side, the surface

    noun, fifth declension · also used · classical · Col. 8.15.3: aquae (Lewis & Short); Plin. NH 9.35 (of a tortoise’s shell) · Declension on Wiktionary

    A post-Augustan word in this sense (Columella, Pliny): the surface of water, of a stone, a shell. In Cicero and the jurists it is a building on another man’s land (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • quī dēmersī sunt in aquā … sī nōn longē absunt ā summō

    those who have gone under the water, if they are not far from the surfaceCic. Fin. 3.48 (Lewis & Short)

  • et operuerant superficiem ejus spīnae

    and thorns had covered its surfaceVulg. Prov. 24.31

See also top, bottom, rubber surface.
